title: Minimize Maximum Pair Sum in Array
description:
# Minimize Maximum Pair Sum in Array

You are given an integer array `nums` with even length. Split every element of `nums` into exactly `nums.length / 2` pairs, so each element is used once.

The sum of a pair is the two values added together. The score of a complete pairing is the largest pair sum among all pairs. Return the smallest possible score over every valid complete pairing.

## Example 1

**Input:** `nums = [3,5,2,3]`

**Output:** `7`

**Explanation:** Sort the values as `[2,3,3,5]`. Pairing `2` with `5` and `3` with `3` gives pair sums `7` and `6`, so the largest pair sum is `7`. No complete pairing can make the largest pair sum smaller.

## Example 2

**Input:** `nums = [3,5,4,2,4,6]`

**Output:** `8`

**Explanation:** After sorting, pair `(2,6)`, `(3,5)`, and `(4,4)`. The pair sums are `8`, `8`, and `8`, so the minimized maximum pair sum is `8`.

## Constraints

* `2 <= nums.length <= 10^5`
* `nums.length` is even.
* `1 <= nums[i] <= 10^9`

solutions.name: Sort Opposite Ends
solutions.description:
## Approach

Sort the array. Then pair the smallest remaining value with the largest remaining value, moving inward until every element is used. Track the maximum sum produced by these opposite-end pairs.

## Key Insight

A largest value should be protected by pairing it with the smallest value still available. If two large values are paired together while two smaller values form another pair, swapping one large value with one small value cannot increase the larger of the two pair sums and usually lowers it. Repeating this exchange leads to opposite-end pairing.

## Complexity Analysis

Sorting dominates the running time. The two-pointer scan is linear and uses only a few integer variables after the in-place sort.

solutions.name: Binary Search on Maximum Pair Sum
solutions.timeComplexity: O(n log n + n log V)
solutions.description:
## Approach

Sort the array once, then binary search the answer value. For a candidate limit, greedily pair the smallest remaining value with the largest remaining value and check whether every pair sum stays at most that limit.

## Key Insight

The feasibility predicate is monotonic: if all pairs can be formed with maximum sum at most `x`, then any larger limit is also feasible. The same opposite-end exchange argument makes the feasibility check exact, so binary search can find the minimum feasible limit.

## Complexity Analysis

The initial sort costs `O(n log n)`. Each feasibility check scans the array once, and the value range contributes `O(log V)` checks, where `V` is the possible pair-sum range.

solutions.name: TreeMap Multiset Pairing
solutions.description:
## Approach

Store value frequencies in a `TreeMap`, which behaves like an ordered multiset. Repeatedly remove one copy of the current smallest value and one copy of the current largest value, then update the maximum pair sum.

## Key Insight

This keeps the same optimal smallest-with-largest greedy invariant without allocating an array by numeric value. That matters because `nums[i]` can be as large as `10^9`, so bucket counting by `max(nums)` is not a valid general solution for this prompt.

## Complexity Analysis

Let `d` be the number of distinct values. Building and updating the ordered multiset costs `O(n log d)` time and `O(d)` extra space.
